sources.entry: Claude Mnemonic by lukaszraczylo - Memory management and retrieval for Claude Code

summary.one_liner: Claude Mnemonic is a local memory plugin for Claude Code that captures observations from coding sessions and injects relevant past knowledge into future sessions.
summary.what_it_does: It hooks into Claude Code sessions to capture what Claude learns, such as bug fixes, architecture decisions, and patterns that work, and stores them in SQLite with full-text search. Semantic search uses local sqlite-vec embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), with optional cross-encoder reranking (BGE reranker) for two-stage retrieval. Observations are scoped per project by default, with tags like best-practice or security promoting them to global scope. It exposes MCP tools for search, timeline, observation management, and admin/analytics actions such as stats, patterns, and maintenance. A web dashboard at localhost:37777 lets you browse and manage memories, and a live statusline shows metrics. The README also describes a knowledge graph, conflict detection, importance scoring with time decay, and automatic updates.
use_cases: Remember codebase context across Claude Code sessions
Recall past bug fixes and architecture decisions
Share best practices across multiple projects
Semantic search over past coding observations
Browse and manage stored memories in a web dashboard
Keep project knowledge separate from global knowledge
notable: Runs entirely locally with local embeddings and reranking; no API keys, uses existing Claude Code subscription
Two-stage retrieval: bi-encoder embeddings plus cross-encoder reranking, configurable via settings
Project vs global scope determined by observation tags
Exposes MCP tools (search, timeline, observation, memory_admin) with action-based subcommands
Web dashboard at localhost:37777 with memory browsing and a knowledge graph view
caveats: Building from source requires Go 1.24+, Node.js 18+, and a CGO-compatible compiler
Platform support listed as macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), Linux amd64/arm64, and Windows amd64
Auto-updates download in the background (up to 250MB) and apply on restart
